title: Lock contention on a hot key range versus capacity exhaustion
tell: Lock wait time rises sharply while traffic is flat or only mildly elevated, which separates contention from load.
The split rate climbs as the balancer reacts to the hot range. That is the system responding to imbalance, not causing it.
Contention concentrates on a small number of cells rather than tracking regional traffic weight, because a hot key lives in one range.
ABORTED responses dominate the error mix; those are retried by clients and may not be user-visible even while the metric looks alarming.

confusable_with.discriminator: Capacity problems raise latency and CPU together and scale with traffic. Contention raises lock wait first and is largely indifferent to request volume.
